reply_text:
Going ahead. First, how the write-time path works today: what the ingest hook runs, and how the model tier that raises sorries gets called.Tests for the parts that make decisions: notice handoff, the shared-home choice, the recurrence wording, and the hook's output shape.The instant notice came straight back into this session on the write. Now waiting for the model tier to finish; its notice should arrive on my next tool call:㊥ Recall at write time works end to end, and I watched it happen in this session. When I saved a memory, minus40 named the related memories in other projects within half a second. About 30 seconds later it told me how they relate and proposed where the lesson should live (minus40 `c984b06`).

㊢ (what happened, live) I acted on its first proposal by merging the Zai quota lessons into my `-home-joe` note:
1. **On the write**, the hook answered at once that my note was close to `zai-seat-allocation` (voxterm, since 09-15) and `proof2-dispatch-pool` (voxterm, since 09-27), "in other projects' memory, which this session does not load".
2. **On my next tool call**, the model tier's verdict arrived: **refines** `zai-seat-allocation`, both saying that exhausted Zai quota makes jobs fail silently. The new note adds the five-hour window, the separate weekly limit and the three-seat cap. It flagged this as a lesson learned before in another project, and proposed keeping one copy in `-home-joe`. That's where it now is.

The relations are also stored in the store as `:memory/relation` edges, so they can be queried later.

㊟ (how far to trust it) The model's verdict is advice, not fact. The quotes it cites are checked word for word against both notes, but its reasoning can still slip. In the first run it blended Kimi's five-hour window with Zai's. I only caught that because I read the September note before merging, so the merged note now keeps the two providers apart. Keeping a person, or the writing agent, in the loop is part of the design: the notice proposes, the writer decides.

㊩ (scope you should know about) The ingest hook is global, so every Claude session that writes a memory now gets these notices, and the model tier runs on Haiku through `claude -p`. I think that's within the direction you approved, but it does change what other agents see. `bg.py kill` with the id in `~/notes/minus40-relate-bg-id.txt` stops the model tier; the instant notice is a few lines in `ingest_hook.py`. Separately, I found that the older drain for sorries isn't running: 17 writes are waiting. I'll restart it after this.

㊭ (next) The row of the table still missing is **answers**: noticing when a new memory resolves an open question (an ArSE thread, or an ask in your inbox). That's where this joins up with ArSE. After that comes recall on your prompts, using the same candidate finder.

previous_reply_acts.text: (why I missed it) I checked how this morning's repeat happened. The September note sits in a different project's memory folder (`-home-joe-code-voxterm/zai-seat-allocation`), so it never appeared in the index my sessions load. Claude Code's memory is split by working directory; minus40 has all 299 memories in one store. So this wasn't carelessness that a duplicate check would catch. The lesson was learned in one place and needed in another. Three memories in three projects touch Zai quota (09-06, 09-15, 09-27), and today's is the fourth.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-15
previous_reply_acts.text: ("like the ArSE") The comparison fits. ArSE is Stack Exchange for agents: questions are kept as legible gaps, answers are evidence. Stack Exchange closes duplicates, because there a repeated question is noise. In a memory, a repeated lesson tells you something about how the knowledge is spread. "Beyond duplicate" then means saying how the new memory relates to the old ones, and what follows from each relation:

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-15
previous_reply_acts.text: (how to build it) Finding candidate related memories is classical: shared entities plus overlap between block facts, across every project. Naming the relation takes a model, through the same write-time path that already raises sorries. The result comes straight back into the writing session from the ingest hook. The first test case is today's Zai pair: it should come back as "refines, re-learned in a fourth project; proposed home: `-home-joe`". I'll start with candidate finding and the re-learning case, unless you'd rather begin with "answers".
